items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ ([[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]], [[def-scheme-over-base]]). An **algebraic cycle** on $X$ is a formal $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $X$ ([[def-integral-scheme]], [[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]); it is **finite** when the combination is finite. For an integer $d$, the **group of $d$-cycles** is the free abelian group
$$Z_d(X):=\bigoplus_{V} \mathbb Z\cdot[V],$$
the direct sum running over the integral closed subschemes $V\subseteq X$ of dimension $d$ ([[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]], [[def-noetherian-topological-space]], [[def-free-abelian-group]]); one writes $Z_*(X)=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}Z_d(X)$. The **support** $|\alpha|$ of a cycle $\alpha=\sum_i n_i[V_i]$ is the union of the $V_i$ with $n_i\ne0$, a closed subset of $X$; a cycle is **effective** if all $n_i\ge0$.

**Conventions.** (i) A cycle class may be represented by a locally finite sum in the situations below; finite sums suffice for the schemes of finite type over a field used in this pair. (ii) All integral closed subschemes are taken with the reduced structure, and $[V]$ denotes the associated basis element; the fundamental cycle of an integral $X$ of dimension $n$ is $[X]\in Z_n(X)$. (iii) For $X$ equidimensional of pure dimension $n$ one writes $A^p(X):=A_{n-p}(X)$ for the codimension-$p$ Chow group once $A_*$ is available (def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence). (iv) No choice is used in this definition beyond the free abelian group on the set of subvarieties ([[def-free-abelian-group]]).
items.local_argument:
Definition. The only points requiring care are: the free abelian group on the set of integral closed subschemes of $X$ of dimension $d$ exists ([[def-free-abelian-group]]); the set is well defined because dimension is a property of the underlying topological space ([[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]]); and the support of a finite combination is closed. Compare Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.1-1.3 and Stacks 42.8 (tag 02QY ff.), whose ``cycles with support'' convention is a mild generalization; we use the classical finite-support version of Fulton, which is what the later constructions in this pair use.

items.statement:
Let $A$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and fraction field $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ ([[def-local-ring]], [[def-noetherian-ring]], [[def-krull-dimension-of-a-ring]], [[def-field-of-fractions]]). For a nonzero $A$-module $M$ of finite length write $\ell_A(M)$ for its length ([[def-composition-series-and-length-of-a-module]]). For $0\ne r\in K$ choose $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$ with $r=a/b$ and set
$$\operatorname{ord}_A(r):=\ell_A(A/aA)-\ell_A(A/bA)\in\mathbb Z.$$
Then:

1. $A/aA$ and $A/bA$ have finite length, so $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)$ is defined; in fact a Noetherian ring of dimension $0$ has finite length, and $A/aA$ has dimension $0$ for $a\ne0$ because every prime of $A/aA$ lies over the unique maximal ideal of the one-dimensional domain $A$.
2. The value $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)$ does not depend on the presentation $r=a/b$: if $a/b=c/d$ with $a,b,c,d\ne0$, then $ad=bc$, and the two exact sequences $0\to A/aA\xrightarrow{\,d\,}A/adA\to A/dA\to0$ and $0\to A/cA\xrightarrow{\,b\,}A/bcA\to A/bA\to0$, together with additivity of length in short exact sequences ([[cor-length-is-additive-in-short-exact-sequences]]), give $\ell(A/aA)-\ell(A/bA)=\ell(A/cA)-\ell(A/dA)$.
3. $\operatorname{ord}_A(rs)=\operatorname{ord}_A(r)+\operatorname{ord}_A(s)$ and $\operatorname{ord}_A(r^{-1})=-\operatorname{ord}_A(r)$ for $r,s\in K^*$; $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)=0$ for $r\in A^*$; $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)\ge0$ for $r\in A$, with equality if and only if $r\in A^*$.
4. If $A$ is a discrete valuation ring with normalized valuation $v_A$ ([[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]), then $\operatorname{ord}_A=v_A$; if $A$ is regular of dimension one, $\operatorname{ord}_A$ is the normalized valuation of the discrete valuation ring $A$ ([[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]]).
items.local_argument:
Elementary. Finiteness of the lengths in (1): $A/aA$ is a Noetherian ring of dimension $0$, hence Artinian, hence of finite length. Claim (2) is the two exact-sequence computation displayed in the statement, using additivity of length ([[cor-length-is-additive-in-short-exact-sequences]]); the maps are injective because $A$ is a domain and $b,d\ne0$. Claim (3) follows by inserting finitely many intermediate terms and using the exact sequence $0\to A/bA\xrightarrow{a}A/abA\to A/aA\to0$, which gives $\ell(A/abA)=\ell(A/aA)+\ell(A/bA)$; the sign and positivity statements follow from $\ell=0\iff$ the quotient vanishes. Claim (4) is immediate from the definitions of length and of the normalized valuation. This is the order function used in Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, A.3 and proved there for arbitrary one-dimensional Noetherian local rings via Herbrand quotients; Stacks 42.2-42.6 (Key Lemma, tag 0EAX) proves the general form. The present lemma is the special case needed to define the divisor of a rational function on an integral closed subscheme (def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence).

items.statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme ([[def-locally-noetherian-and-noetherian-scheme]]). Then the category of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules is abelian ([[thm-coherent-sheaves-abelian-noetherian-scheme]], [[def-coherent-module-scheme]]), and the category of finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules of locally constant rank is an exact category ([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]).

1. The **Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves** $K_0(X):=K_0(\operatorname{Coh}(X))$ is the abelian group with one generator $[\mathcal F]$ for each coherent sheaf, subject to $[\mathcal F]=[\mathcal F']+[\mathcal F'']$ for every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]]); existence of the group is the group completion of the commutative monoid modulo the exact-sequence relations.
2. The **Grothendieck group of vector bundles** $K^0(X)$ is the abelian group with one generator $[\mathcal E]$ for each finite locally free sheaf of locally constant rank, subject to $[\mathcal E]=[\mathcal E']+[\mathcal E'']$ for every exact sequence $0\to\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E''\to0$ of such sheaves. Tensor product makes $K^0(X)$ a commutative ring with unit $[\mathcal O_X]$ ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]], [[lem-tensor-qc-modules-quasi-coherent]]), and makes $K_0(X)$ a $K^0(X)$-module via $[\mathcal E]\cdot[\mathcal F]:=[\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F]$, using that tensoring with a locally free sheaf is exact.
3. Every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of locally Noetherian schemes induces $f^*:K^0(Y)\to K^0(X)$ by pullback of locally free sheaves ([[lem-pullback-qc-module-quasi-coherent]], [[lem-dual-locally-free-and-base-change]]); flat $f$ also induces $f^*:K_0(Y)\to K_0(X)$.
4. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper, the higher direct images $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ are coherent ([[thm-proper-pushforward-coherent]]) and vanish for $q\gg0$ over affine opens of $Y$ ([[thm-serre-finiteness-projective-cohomology]]); the resulting pushforward $f_!:K_0(X)\to K_0(Y)$ is defined in def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory.
5. The natural map $K^0(X)\to K_0(X)$, $[\mathcal E]\mapsto[\mathcal E]$, is well defined and additive; it is an isomorphism when $X$ is a regular quasi-projective scheme of finite type over a field (lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves).
items.local_argument: Definitions together with the standard exactness properties. For (3), pullback of a locally free sheaf is locally free and pullback preserves exact sequences of locally free sheaves ([[lem-pullback-qc-module-quasi-coherent]]), so $f^*$ is defined; for flat $f$, pullback of a short exact sequence of coherent sheaves is exact ($-\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal O_X$ is exact when $\mathcal O_X$ is flat over $\mathcal O_Y$), so $f^*$ is defined on $K_0$. For (2), tensoring a short exact sequence of coherent sheaves with a locally free sheaf is exact, so the $K^0$-action is well defined; the ring axioms are those of the tensor product. Reference: Stacks 42.69 (Appendix B: rational equivalence and $K$-groups, tag 0AYD) and Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 4-5 (the Grothendieck groups of coherent and locally free sheaves and their ring structure), and Vakil 245 Class 18 Section 2.2 (definitions of $K_0X$ and $K^0X$, functoriality, module structure, projection formula).

items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$. For $d\in\mathbb Z$ let $\operatorname{Rat}_d(X)\subseteq Z_d(X)$ be the subgroup generated by all cycles of the form
$$(i_W)_*\operatorname{div}(r),\qquad \operatorname{div}(r)=\sum_{V\subseteq W}\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{W,V}}(r)\,[V],$$
where $W\subseteq X$ is an integral closed subscheme of dimension $d+1$ ([[def-integral-scheme]]), $i_W:W\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion, $r\in k(W)^*$ is a nonzero rational function on $W$ ([[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]], [[def-field-of-fractions]]), the sum runs over the integral closed subschemes $V\subseteq W$ of dimension $d$, and $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{W,V}}(r)$ is the order function of [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]] for the one-dimensional Noetherian local domain $\mathcal O_{W,V}$ ([[def-local-ring]]). The sum is finite: a cycle on $W$ has finite support, equivalently the set of codimension-one points of $W$ at which $r$ has nonzero order is finite. The elements of $\operatorname{Rat}_d(X)$ are the $d$-cycles **rationally equivalent to zero**; two cycles are **rationally equivalent** if their difference is, written $\alpha\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}\beta$. The **Chow group of $d$-cycles** is
$$A_d(X):=Z_d(X)/\operatorname{Rat}_d(X),\qquad A_*(X)=\bigoplus_{d}A_d(X).$$

**Basic facts.** (i) Rational equivalence is an equivalence relation compatible with the group structure, by definition. (ii) If $W$ is a *normal* integral closed subscheme, then $\operatorname{div}(r)$ agrees with the principal Weil divisor of $r$ computed with the divisor theory of [[def-order-codimension-one-rational-function]], [[def-principal-weil-divisor-and-class-group]]; in particular for $X$ integral of dimension $n$ and normal (e.g. smooth), $A_n(X)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by $[X]$ and $A_d(X)=0$ for $d>\dim X$. (iii) For $X$ equidimensional of pure dimension $n$, set $A^p(X):=A_{n-p}(X)$; this is the codimension grading used throughout. (iv) Equivalent presentation: $\alpha\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}0$ if and only if $\alpha=\sum_i (i_{W_i})_*\operatorname{div}(r_i)$ as above; this is the "Fulton 1.6" definition with supports on closed subschemes of $X\times\mathbb P^1$ specialized, and it is Stacks' Definition 42.19.1 (tag 02RW).
items.local_argument:
Definition plus consistency checks. The subgroup $\operatorname{Rat}_d(X)$ is generated by the displayed cycles, so rational equivalence is well defined once the order function is; finiteness of the support of a divisor uses that the residue field at each codimension-one point of a $d+1$-dimensional integral noetherian subscheme is nonzero and only finitely many orders are nonzero, which follows from the finiteness of the localizations of a nonzero function (Stacks Lemma 42.17.x, tag 02RT). Fact (ii) is [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]](4) applied over the normal points; for normal $W$ the local rings $\mathcal O_{W,V}$ are discrete valuation rings ([[def-order-codimension-one-rational-function]]), so the order function is the valuation and $\operatorname{div}$ is the principal divisor of [[def-principal-weil-divisor-and-class-group]]. The remaining assertions are restatements of the definition. The general reference is Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.3 (p. 10) and 1.6; Stacks 42.19.1 (tag 02RW) and Lemma 42.19.3 (tag 02RX) for the localization exact sequence used in lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space.

items.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over a field; use finite cycles if $X$ is of finite type, and locally finite cycles otherwise. For each integer $d$, a coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ whose support has dimension at most $d$ has the $d$-cycle
$$[\mathcal F]_d=\sum_{\dim V=d}\ell_{\mathcal O_{X,\eta_V}}(\mathcal F_{\eta_V})[V],$$
where $V$ runs over the integral closed subschemes and $\eta_V$ is their generic point. The sum is locally finite, and finite for finite type $X$; its terms are precisely the dimension-$d$ components of the support. In any short exact sequence of coherent sheaves all supported in dimension at most $d$, these $d$-cycles are additive. No additivity is claimed for the sum of cycles in all dimensions when the supports change.
For a closed subscheme $Y$, define its fundamental cycle $[Y]$ by summing the generic lengths at every irreducible component of $Y$. If $Y$ is pure dimensional of dimension $d$, $[Y]=[\mathcal O_Y]_d$. For reduced $Y$ every component coefficient is one.
For flat $f:X'\to X$ of pure relative dimension $r$, $[f^{-1}Y]_{d+r}=f^*[Y]_d$ when $Y$ is pure of dimension $d$. If $Y$ is pure of dimension $d$ and the local equation of an effective Cartier divisor $D$ of $X$ is a nonzerodivisor on $\mathcal O_Y$, then $D|_Y$ is an effective Cartier divisor and its cycle is the fundamental $(d-1)$-cycle of $Y\cap D$. The nonzerodivisor condition cannot be replaced by $Y\not\subset D$: it must exclude every associated point of $Y$, including embedded ones.
items.local_argument: At a dimension-$d$ point of the support of a coherent sheaf supported in dimension at most $d$, localization has zero-dimensional support, so the localized finite module has finite length. There are only finitely many such generic support points. Localization is exact and length is additive, proving additivity for sheaves with the common dimension bound. For an integral or reduced subscheme the generic local rings are fields, giving multiplicity one. For flat pullback, localize at a generic point of a component of the inverse image. A composition series of the finite-length module at the original generic point remains exact after flat tensor, and each simple factor becomes the residue-field fibre module. Additivity of length gives the pulled-back coefficient, including the generic fibre multiplicity. For the divisor assertion, its equation is injective on $\mathcal O_Y$ by hypothesis; its quotient is $\mathcal O_{Y\cap D}$, so the order/length coefficient defining the Cartier cycle is exactly its generic length. Source: Stacks 42.9-42.10 and 42.14, with fixed-dimension bounds essential. Example showing the omitted bound is false: on an integral curve $C$, $0\to\mathcal O_C(-p)\to\mathcal O_C\to\mathcal O_p\to0$ has full support cycles $[C],[C],[p]$, which are not additive in the cycle group.

items.statement:
Let $X$ be a regular quasi-projective scheme of finite type over a field. Then the natural map
$$K^0(X)\longrightarrow K_0(X),\qquad [\mathcal E]\longmapsto[\mathcal E]$$
is an isomorphism. Every coherent sheaf has a finite resolution by finite locally free sheaves, and its class corresponds to the alternating sum of such a resolution, independent of the resolution. Consequently this identification applies to every smooth quasi-projective variety used in the Riemann-Roch theorem of this page. Regularity alone is not asserted to supply a global vector-bundle resolution on an arbitrary scheme.
items.local_argument: Use the complete finite-resolution and Grothendieck-group argument of Borel-Serre 1958 §4, Théorème 2, including Lemma 10. Quasi-projectivity supplies an ample invertible sheaf: after extending a coherent sheaf to a projective closure, a sufficiently large twist is generated by finitely many global sections, so untwisting gives a finite locally free sheaf surjecting onto it. Its kernel is coherent, allowing iteration. At each local regular ring, successive kernels lower projective dimension; after at most $\dim X$ iterations the kernel is locally free. Thus the iteration terminates in a finite locally free resolution. The alternating-resolution construction and its independence/additivity are the Grothendieck-group argument of §4, not the false identification of perfect-complex K-theory with vector-bundle K-theory without a resolution-property hypothesis. All consumers use quasi-projective schemes, including projective bundles and blowups of their smooth centres. Stacks 42.58.1 is not accepted as a proof of the previously stated arbitrary-regular resolution-property claim.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice, inherited from the coherence and finiteness suppliers below ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over $k$ ([[def-proper-morphism]], [[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]]); then $Y$ is locally Noetherian and for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ all higher direct images $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ are coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules ([[thm-proper-pushforward-coherent]], [[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]]) and vanish for all sufficiently large $q$ ([[thm-serre-finiteness-projective-cohomology]] over affine opens of $Y$, the vanishing being local on $Y$). Set
$$f_![\mathcal F]:=\sum_{q\ge0}(-1)^q\,[R^qf_*\mathcal F]\in K_0(Y)$$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]). Then:

1. $f_!$ is a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(X)\to K_0(Y)$ of abelian groups: a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ on $X$ induces the long exact sequence of higher direct images $0\to f_*\mathcal F'\to f_*\mathcal F\to f_*\mathcal F''\to R^1f_*\mathcal F'\to\cdots$ ([[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]], [[cor-derived-long-exact-sequence]]), whose alternating sum is zero, giving $f_![\mathcal F]=f_![\mathcal F']+f_![\mathcal F'']$.
2. (Functoriality) $\operatorname{id}_!=\operatorname{id}$ and $(g\circ f)_!=g_!\circ f_!$ for composable proper morphisms: the Leray spectral sequence for the composition degenerates after the alternating sum because only finitely many terms in each bidegree are nonzero ([[thm-leray-spectral-sequence-for-sheaf-cohomology]]).
3. (Compatibility with the module structure) $f_!(f^*[\mathcal E]\cdot[\mathcal F])=[\mathcal E]\cdot f_![\mathcal F]$ for $\mathcal E$ locally free on $Y$ and $\mathcal F$ coherent on $X$, i.e. the projection formula; this is proved in lem-projection-formula-in-algebraic-k-theory. For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $X$ projective, $f_![\mathcal F]=\chi(X,\mathcal F)$ is the Euler characteristic ([[def-euler-characteristic-coherent-sheaf]]).
items.local_argument: Definitions and standard homological algebra, following Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 3 (the direct image of a coherent sheaf and the theorem on the coherence/finiteness of the higher direct images) and 5 (pushforward on $K$ and its functoriality), and Vakil 245 Class 18 Section 2.2 (definition $f_*[\mathcal F]=\sum(-1)^i[R^if_*\mathcal F]$, projection formula, functoriality). Well-definedness: the long exact sequence of higher direct images is the standard long exact sequence for a short exact sequence of complexes in the derived category; the alternating sum of its terms is zero because the sequence has finitely many nonzero terms, using the coherence and higher vanishing of the $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ ([[thm-proper-pushforward-coherent]], [[thm-serre-finiteness-projective-cohomology]]). Functoriality: the Leray spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=R^pg_*(R^qf_*\mathcal F)\Rightarrow R^{p+q}(g\circ f)_*\mathcal F$ ([[thm-leray-spectral-sequence-for-sheaf-cohomology]]) has finitely supported rows and columns (coherence plus the vanishing statements), so the alternating sum of $E_\infty$ equals the alternating sum of the total derived images, giving $g_!f_!= (g\circ f)_!$. Point 3 is lem-projection-formula-in-algebraic-k-theory.

items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over $k$ ([[def-proper-morphism]], [[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]]). For an integral closed subscheme $V\subseteq X$ with generic point $\eta$, let $W=\overline{f(V)}\subseteq Y$ with the reduced structure, an integral closed subscheme ([[def-scheme-theoretic-image]], [[thm-proper-morphism-closed-image]]). Define
$$f_*[V]:=\begin{cases} [k(V):k(W)]\cdot[W], & \dim W=\dim V,\\ 0, & \dim W<\dim V,\end{cases}$$
where $k(V)$, $k(W)$ are the function fields ([[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]] or [[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]]) and $[k(V):k(W)]$ is the extension degree ([[def-extension-degree-and-finite-extension]]), finite because a dominant morphism $V\to W$ of integral finite-type $k$-schemes with $\dim V=\dim W$ has algebraic, hence finite, function field extension. Extending $\mathbb Z$-linearly gives $f_*:Z_d(X)\to Z_d(Y)$ for all $d$. Then:

1. $f_*$ is a homomorphism of graded groups and $f_*(\operatorname{Rat}_d(X))\subseteq \operatorname{Rat}_d(Y)$, so it descends to $f_*:A_d(X)\to A_d(Y)$ ([[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]]).
2. (Functoriality) $\operatorname{id}_*=\operatorname{id}$ and $(g\circ f)_*=g_*\circ f_*$ for proper $f,g$; the degree is multiplicative in towers of finite function-field extensions.
3. (Base change) For a cartesian square with flat $g$ and proper $f$, the compatibility of lem-pushforward-pullback-compatibility-chow holds.
4. (Normalization) If $f$ is finite flat of constant degree $n$ between integral schemes of the same dimension, then $f_*[X]=n[Y]$.

Point (1) is the nontrivial assertion: for $W\subseteq X$ integral of dimension $d+1$ and $r\in k(W)^*$ one has
$$f_*\bigl(\operatorname{div}_W(r)\bigr)=\operatorname{div}_{f(W)}\bigl(N_{k(W)/k(f(W))}(r)\bigr)$$
when $\dim f(W)=\dim W$, and $f_*(\operatorname{div}_W(r))=0$ when $\dim f(W)<\dim W$; here $N$ is the field norm.
items.local_argument:
Follow Stacks 42.11-42.12 (tags 02R3-02R4) for the definition and the reduction of the norm identity, and Stacks 42.18 (tag 02RS) and Lemma 42.20.3 (tag 02S0) for the well-definedness of $f_*$ on Chow groups; the displayed norm identity is Stacks Lemma 42.18.3. The key local computation is: for a codimension-one point $V$ of $W$ lying over a codimension-one point $U$ of $W'=f(W)$, the local degree $[k(V):k(U)]$ and the order functions satisfy $\operatorname{ord}_{U}(N(r))=\sum_{V\mapsto U}\operatorname{ord}_{V}(r)\,[k(V):k(U)]$, proved by reducing to the case of a one-dimensional local domain via [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]] (Stacks Lemma 42.18.1-42.18.2); the sum is finite and the unramified-in-codimension-one case follows from the norm's behaviour on DVRs. Functoriality (2) is Stacks Lemma 42.12.2 and the multiplicativity of extension degrees (thm-multiplicativity-of-separable-degree for the separable part, def-inseparable-degree for the rest). Compare Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.4, and Vakil 245 Classes 2-4, where the same norm computation is written out.

For completeness the dimension-drop case in the displayed divisor formula has two parts. If $\dim f(W)<\dim W-1$, each divisor component drops dimension and pushes to zero. If $\dim f(W)=\dim W-1$, the coefficient at the image is the degree of the principal divisor on the proper generic fibre curve. Pass to its finite normalization, with residue-field weights in the norm/length formula. A nonconstant rational function on that normal proper curve extends to a finite map to $\mathbb P^1$; its zero and pole fibres have the same degree (the generic field degree), so that degree is zero. A constant function has zero divisor. Thus the coefficient vanishes. No nonzero principal divisor on the image is used when the function-field extension is transcendental.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over a field $k$ ([[def-proper-morphism]], [[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]]). Let $\mathcal E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module ([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then for every $q\ge0$ there is a canonical isomorphism of coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules
$$R^qf_*\bigl(f^*\mathcal E\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\bigr)\;\cong\;\mathcal E\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}R^qf_*\mathcal F,$$
and consequently, in $K_0(Y)$ ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]),
$$f_!\bigl(f^*[\mathcal E]\cdot[\mathcal F]\bigr)=[\mathcal E]\cdot f_![\mathcal F],$$
where $f_!$ is the pushforward of [[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]] and the products are the $K$-theory module products.
items.local_argument: Standard projection formula for higher direct images: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ over which $\mathcal E$ is free, the formula reduces to the case $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_Y$, where it is the naturality of $f_*$; the general case follows by additivity and local trivialization, since locally free sheaves are a direct summand locally ([[lem-internal-hom-fp-qc]] gives the internal-hom adjunction that produces the canonical map, and the trace/evaluation argument shows it is an isomorphism). Summing over $q$ with alternating signs gives the $K$-theory identity, since $[\mathcal E]$ acts on $K_0$ by tensor product.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field.

1. In $K^0(\mathbb P^n_k)=K_0(\mathbb P^n_k)$ ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]], [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]) the classes $[\mathcal O(i)]$, $0\le i\le n$, form a $\mathbb Z$-basis; equivalently $K_0(\mathbb P^n)=\mathbb Z^{n+1}$ generated by the twisting sheaves ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]], [[thm-twisting-sheaf-invertible-standard-graded]]).
2. For every locally Noetherian $k$-scheme $Y$ and every $n\ge0$, the exterior-product map
$$K_0(Y)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K_0(\mathbb P^n_k)\longrightarrow K_0(\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY)$$
is surjective; here $K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)$ is the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]) and the product is $[\mathcal F]\times[\mathcal G]\mapsto[\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal F\otimes\mathrm{pr}_2^*\mathcal G]$ ([[lem-tensor-qc-modules-quasi-coherent]], [[lem-pullback-qc-module-quasi-coherent]]).
3. More generally, if $\mathcal E$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module of rank $r+1$, the projective bundle $\mathbb P(\mathcal E)$ has $K_0(\mathbb P(\mathcal E))$ generated over $K_0(Y)$ by $1,[\mathcal O(1)],\dots,[\mathcal O(r)]$, via the relative-diagonal Koszul computation; no global cell decomposition of a nontrivial bundle is assumed ([[def-projective-bundle-scheme]]).
items.local_argument:
For a rank-$r$ bundle $E$ and $q:P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(E)\to Y$, use the relative diagonal in $P\times_Y P$, with tautological line $L_1$ on the first factor and quotient $Q_2$ on the second. Its equation is the section of $L_1^\vee\otimes Q_2$ induced by $L_1\to q^*E\to Q_2$. On two affine fibre charts it is the sequence of differences of the $r-1$ fibre coordinates, so its Koszul complex resolves the diagonal. For every coherent $F$ on $P$, that Koszul complex remains exact after tensor with $\operatorname{pr}_1^*F$: the differences are a regular sequence on the polynomial module obtained from $F$, by successive evaluation in the second fibre coordinates. Its terms are $\operatorname{pr}_1^*(F(-j))\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*\bigwedge^jQ^\vee$. Push to the second factor; flat base change and the projection formula, checked on the finite standard projective affine Čech cover, give
$$[F]=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}(-1)^j q^*q_![F(-j)]\otimes[\bigwedge^jQ^\vee].$$
The tautological dual exact sequence gives $[\bigwedge^jQ^\vee]=\sum_{a=0}^j(-1)^a q^*[\bigwedge^{j-a}E^\vee][\mathcal O(a)]$, by its exterior filtration. Thus these terms are sums of $q^*$ of coherent classes tensored with $\mathcal O(a)$ for $0\le a<r$. This works on locally Noetherian bases: higher direct images are coherent locally and vanish above fibre dimension, and the equality is the global sheaf/Čech computation, not gluing local Grothendieck-group identities. Dualizing $E$ gives the quotient convention. This proves both generation assertions including nontrivial projective bundles.
For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$, independence of $\mathcal O(0),\ldots,\mathcal O(n)$ follows by pairing with the Euler characteristics of twists $\mathcal O(-j)$ for $j=0,\ldots,n$: the matrix $\chi(\mathcal O(a-j))=\binom{n+a-j}{n}$ is upper triangular with diagonal one, since $-n\le a-j<0$ gives zero. The standard projective affine Čech complex computes these Euler characteristics. Generation plus this unimodular pairing proves the asserted basis. AC is inherited from coherent cohomology. Borel-Serre §9 and Vakil19 supply comparison for the trivial bundle case; their cellular argument alone does not prove the general-bundle claim. The diagonal calculation is given in full here and agrees with the later smooth-base helper.

items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a flat morphism of schemes locally of finite type over $k$ ([[def-flat-morphism-schemes]]) all of whose nonempty fibres have pure dimension $n$ ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]], [[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]]); for instance $f$ smooth of relative dimension $n$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]], [[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]], [[lem-smooth-fibres-smooth]]) or an open immersion with $n=0$. For an integral closed subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ let $f^{-1}(V)=V\times_Y X$ be the scheme-theoretic preimage and let $[f^{-1}(V)]$ be its cycle ([[lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme]]). Extending linearly gives $f^*:Z_d(Y)\to Z_{d+n}(X)$. Then:

1. $f^{-1}(V)$ is equidimensional of dimension $\dim V+n$, so $f^*[V]$ is a pure $(d+n)$-cycle; this is the only place the pure-fibre-dimension hypothesis is used.
2. $f^*(\operatorname{Rat}_d(Y))\subseteq\operatorname{Rat}_{d+n}(X)$: for an integral closed subscheme $W\subseteq Y$ of dimension $d+1$ and $r\in k(W)^*$, the pulled back rational function $f^*r$ on $f^{-1}(W)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}_{f^{-1}(W)}(f^*r)=f^*(\operatorname{div}_W(r))$, and the right-hand side lies in $\operatorname{Rat}_{d+n}(X)$.
3. Consequently $f^*$ descends to a graded homomorphism $f^*:A_d(Y)\to A_{d+n}(X)$ ([[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]]).
4. (Functoriality) $\operatorname{id}^*=\operatorname{id}$ and $(g\circ f)^*=f^*\circ g^*$ for composable flat morphisms of the stated kind; if $f$ is an open immersion then $f^*$ is the restriction of cycles.
5. (Localization) If $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion and $i:Z=X\setminus U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary reduced closed subscheme, the sequence $A_*(Z)\xrightarrow{i_*}A_*(X)\xrightarrow{j^*}A_*(U)\to0$ is exact (using [[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]] for $i_*$).
items.local_argument:
Follow Stacks 42.13-42.14 (tag 02RA) and Lemma 42.20.2 (tag 02RZ?) for well-definedness, and Lemma 42.19.3 (tag 02RX) for the localization sequence in (5); Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.7 for the classical statement. (1) is the flat fibre-dimension statement: for $f$ flat and locally of finite type with fibres of pure dimension $n$, the preimage of an integral closed subscheme is equidimensional of dimension $\dim V+n$ (Stacks Lemma 42.13.1-42.13.3; compare [[thm-flat-families-fibre-dimension-locally-constant]], which supplies the locally-constant fibre dimension in the proper flat case). (2) reduces fibrewise: over an affine chart with $f$ given by a flat ring map $A\to B$, the divisor of $f^*r$ is computed by the image of a principal divisor under the flat map, and multiplicities are preserved by flatness (Stacks Lemma 42.14.2). (4) is Stacks Lemma 42.14.4. The hypothesis of pure fibre dimension cannot be dropped: see cex-arbitrary-pullback-does-not-define-a-chow-operation for the failure of preimage cycles when fibre dimensions jump.

items.statement: Let $A$ be a two-dimensional local domain essentially of finite type over a field and $f,g\in\operatorname{Frac}(A)^\times$. For each height-one prime $q$, define $\partial_q(f,g)$ by normalization and norms of the DVR symbols $(-1)^{v(f)v(g)}f^{v(g)}/g^{v(f)}$ reduced in the residue fields. Then $\sum_q\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}(\partial_q(f,g))=0$. The difference between two orders of Cartier/rational-section intersection is consequently a sum of divisors of these symbols, supported on the common intersection. This proves well-definedness of first Chern operators and Cartier Gysin on rational equivalence and commutation of two Cartier Gysins.
items.local_argument:
Source: full Stacks42.2-42.6 and 42.27-42.30, with the finite-type normalization simplification. Define $e(M,a,b)=\ell(\ker(a)/bM)-\ell(\ker(b)/aM)$ for the two-periodic complex with $abM=0$ and closed-point-supported homology. The long exact homology sequence proves additivity. If $M$ has finite length then $\ell\ker(a)=\ell M-\ell aM$ and $\ell\ker(b)=\ell M-\ell bM$, so $e=0$. Finite-length changes in a module therefore change no $e$. If $M$ is a lattice in $A_q/(\pi^{u+v})$ for a nonzerodivisor $\pi$ in the one-dimensional localization, then $e(M,\pi^u,\pi^v)=0$: both kernels are the lattices in the complementary powers of $\pi$, and the kernel/image length difference is the same in each parity. For an endomorphism $z$ nonzero at $q$ on a module generically of length $h$ at $q$, $e(M,0,z)=h\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}(z)$; a generic composition filtration, lifted to lattices with only finite-length defects, reduces to the rank-one order/length definition. Exact kernel-image sequences for changing one differential by a multiplier give
$e(M,u\pi^e,v\pi^f)=e(M,\pi^e,\pi^f)-e(\pi^eM,0,u)+e(\pi^fM,0,v)$.
These sequences are obtained by factoring $u\pi^e$ and comparing the images and kernels of $\pi^e$ and $u$; their finite-length connecting terms cancel by additivity of length. The same calculation for multiplying both differentials by $c$ gives $e(M,ca,cb)=e(M,a,b)-e(aM,0,c)+e(bM,0,c)$. Thus denominators can be cleared without changing the resulting symbol formula.
Normalize the two-dimensional finite-type local domain; its normalization is finite and semilocal. In a normal local factor every height-one localization is a DVR. For nonzero $a,b$, the complex on $A/(ab)$ is acyclic by cancellation of $a,b$ in the domain. Map $A/(ab)$ to the direct sum of its image lattices $M_q$ in $A_q/(ab)$ over primes dividing $ab$; this is an isomorphism at each nonmaximal point of the support, so its kernel and cokernel have finite length. Hence $\sum_qe(M_q,a,b)=0$. Write $a=u_q\pi_q^{e_q}$, $b=v_q\pi_q^{f_q}$. The preceding identities, clearing denominators when necessary, give $e(M_q,a,b)=-\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}(u_q^{f_q}v_q^{-e_q})$; the constant sign in the tame symbol has order zero. This proves reciprocity in the normal case. For the original domain, the norm-order formula for the finite normalization identifies the sum of these local identities with its desired sum, weighting residue extensions correctly. That formula follows from the determinant/length calculation of the proper pushforward supplier, and also supplies consistency of this normalized definition with the length order on a nonnormal height-one ring. Bilinearity and additive order extend the result from elements to fractions.
To apply it geometrically, choose rational sections of two line bundles and local generators along their codimension-one divisor components; write them as $f_q,g_q$ times these generators. At each codimension-two point the difference between the two iterated divisor cycles is the sum of the local orders of $\partial_q(f_q,g_q)$, by expanding the section divisors in those generators. The local reciprocity identity makes this the cycle $\sum_q\operatorname{div}_{\overline q}(\partial_q(f_q,g_q))$. Choose a generator to equal the regular section on components outside its zero scheme. There its coefficient is one, hence the corresponding symbol is one, so this principal-divisor discrepancy is supported on the common zero scheme. It is a rational equivalence there and proves Cartier commutation. With the second line bundle trivial and its rational section a rational function, its Chern operation is zero; the same calculation says Cartier Gysin kills principal divisors. Without a support restriction the double-section calculation proves descent of the first Chern operation. This is the exact local key-lemma use needed by the following items.

items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc} X' & \xrightarrow{g'} & X\\ \downarrow f' & & \downarrow f\\ Y' & \xrightarrow{g} & Y\end{array}$$
be a cartesian square of schemes locally of finite type over $k$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]), with $f$ proper (hence $f'$ proper, [[lem-base-change-open-closed-immersions]]) and $g$ flat of relative dimension $n$ with all fibres of pure dimension $n$ (hence $g'$ flat of relative dimension $n$, [[lem-flat-morphisms-stable-base-change]]). Then the two graded homomorphisms $A_d(X)\to A_{d+n}(Y')$ agree:
$$g^*\circ f_*\;=\;f'_*\circ g'^*,$$
where $f_*,f'_*$ are proper pushforwards ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]) and $g^*,g'^*$ are flat pullbacks ([[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]]).
items.local_argument:
Follow Stacks Lemma 42.15.1 (tag 02RF, ``push and pull''), Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, Proposition 1.7.1, and Vakil 245 Class 4 (``proper pushforward commutes with flat pullback''). Reduce to a cycle $\alpha=[V]$, $V\subseteq X$ integral. If $\dim f(V)<\dim V$ then both sides vanish. Otherwise put $W=\overline{f(V)}$ and compute both sides on the components of $V\times_W (W\times_Y Y')$ using the flatness of $g$ (the preimage of $W$ is the underlying set of $W\times_Y Y'$ with multiplicities all equal to $1$ because $g$ is flat and the local rings of $W\times_YY'$ over $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ are flat) and the multiplicativity of extension degrees in the cartesian field diagram $k(V)\otimes_{k(W)}k(W')\to k(V')$. Both sides then equal $\sum [k(V_i):k(W')]\cdot[W_i']$ over the components. The remaining assertions are the functoriality of flat pullback and the base-change stability of properness.

items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-invertible-sheaf]]).

1. **Integral case.** Let $W\subseteq X$ be integral of dimension $n$, with function field $k(W)$ ([[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]], [[def-field-of-fractions]]), and let $s$ be a nonzero rational section of $L|_W$ ([[def-rational-section-line-bundle]]). The **Weil divisor of $s$** is
$$\operatorname{div}_L(s)=\sum_{Z\subseteq W}\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{W,Z}}(s)[Z]\in Z_{n-1}(W),$$
the sum over the codimension-one integral closed subschemes $Z\subseteq W$, with the order function of [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]] read on a local generator of $L$ at the generic point of $Z$; the sum has finite support. The **first Chern class class** $c_1(L)\cap[W]:=[\operatorname{div}_L(s)]\in A_{n-1}(W)$ is independent of the chosen nonzero rational section (two such differ by a rational function, whose divisor is rationally equivalent to zero), and therefore defines a codimension-one Chow class; on a smooth $W$ this is the first Chern class in its Chow ring.
2. **General case.** For an integral closed subscheme $i:W\hookrightarrow X$ of dimension $d+1$ set $c_1(L)\cap[W]:=i_*\bigl(c_1(i^*L)\cap[W]\bigr)\in A_d(X)$, where $i_*$ is the proper pushforward ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]); extend $\mathbb Z$-linearly. The resulting operation $c_1(L)\cap-:A_{d+1}(X)\to A_d(X)$ is well defined on Chow groups (this is the content of the next two references) and graded.

**Basic properties.** (i) $c_1(L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}N)\cap\alpha=(c_1(L)+c_1(N))\cap\alpha$ and $c_1(\mathcal O_X)\cap\alpha=0$ for all $\alpha$. (ii) If $X$ is pure of dimension $d+1$ and a global section $s$ of $L$ is a nonzerodivisor on $\mathcal O_X$, its zero scheme $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor and $c_1(L)\cap[X]=[D]$ in $A_d(X)$. More generally the same formula on a pure-dimensional closed subscheme $Y$ requires $s|_Y$ to be a nonzerodivisor on $\mathcal O_Y$. (iii) $c_1(L)\cap-$ commutes with proper pushforward and flat pullback: for $f:X\to Y$ proper, $f_*(c_1(f^*L)\cap\alpha)=c_1(L)\cap f_*\alpha$, and for $f$ flat of relative dimension $n$, $f^*(c_1(L)\cap\alpha)=c_1(f^*L)\cap f^*\alpha$. (iv) $c_1(L)$ depends only on the isomorphism class of $L$.

**Cartier Gysin.** For a section $s$ of $L$ with zero scheme $j:D\hookrightarrow X$, after any base change define $j^!:A_m(X')\to A_{m-1}(D')$ on integral $V\subset X'$ by the Cartier divisor of $s|_V$ if $V$ is not contained in $D'$, and by $c_1(L|_V)\cap[V]$ if it is; push this class from $D'\cap V$ to $D'$. This works even when the pulled-back zero divisor is not Cartier. It commutes with proper pushforward and flat pullback, two Cartier Gysins commute, and $j^!j_*\beta=c_1(L|_D)\cap\beta$.
items.local_argument: A rational section exists by trivializing the line at the integral generic point. A ratio of choices is a rational function, so the order-function identity changes its divisor only by a principal divisor. Product sections give additivity. The cycle of a regular section is given by lengths of its one-dimensional local quotient by the equation, agreeing with the order definition. Proper and flat compatibilities are the norm-order and flat-length formulas already established for cycle operations; for cycles contained in the zero scheme they give the first Chern projection and pullback identities instead. Descent on rational equivalence uses [[lem-two-dimensional-tame-symbol-reciprocity]]: the rational-section intersection discrepancy is a sum of principal divisors and is zero in Chow. Cartier Gysin has the same two cycle cases. Its image of a principal divisor is the intersection with $c_1(1)=0$, by the same symbol calculation supported on $D$. Hence it descends. The support-controlled double-section discrepancy proves commutation of Cartier Gysins. On a cycle already on $D$, the definition gives exactly $j^!j_*\beta=c_1(L|_D)\beta$. Thus the divisor Gysin required by specialization is supplied explicitly.

items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$. Then for every $d$:
$$A_d(\mathbb P^n_k)=\begin{cases}\mathbb Z\cdot[\mathbb P^d], & 0\le d\le n,\\ 0, & \text{otherwise},\end{cases}$$
where $\mathbb P^d\subseteq\mathbb P^n$ is a $d$-dimensional linear subspace and $[\mathbb P^d]$ its class ([[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]], [[def-algebraic-cycle-and-cycle-group]]). In particular the degree homomorphism
$$\deg:A_0(\mathbb P^n_k)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\mathbb Z,\qquad \sum_x m_x[x]\longmapsto\sum_x m_x[\kappa(x):k\bigr],$$
is an isomorphism; its inverse sends $1$ to $[\mathbb P^0]$ for any $k$-rational point, and every $0$-cycle whose support consists of $k$-rational points has class $(\sum_x m_x)\,[\mathbb P^0]$. For $k=\mathbb C$ this is the classical cellular decomposition. More generally, $A_*(\mathbb A^n_k)$ has $A_0(\mathbb A^n_k)=0$ and $A_d(\mathbb A^n_k)=0$ for $d>0$, since every cycle on affine space is cut down by principal divisors of linear functions (this is the $n=1$ case of [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]] transport).
items.local_argument:
Induction on $n$ using the localization sequence of [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]](5) for the open immersion $j:\mathbb A^n=\mathbb P^n\setminus\mathbb P^{n-1}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n$ and the closed immersion $i:\mathbb P^{n-1}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n$: the sequence $A_d(\mathbb P^{n-1})\xrightarrow{i_*}A_d(\mathbb P^n)\xrightarrow{j^*}A_d(\mathbb A^n)\to0$ is exact (Stacks Lemma 42.19.3, tag 02RX). If $A_*(\mathbb A^n)=0$ in positive degrees and $A_0(\mathbb A^n)=0$, then $i_*$ is surjective, and induction gives that the classes of linear subspaces generate. The affine statement: by homotopy invariance $A_*(\mathbb A^n)\cong A_*(\operatorname{Spec}k)=\mathbb Z$ placed in degree $0$ (Stacks 42.21, and [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]] for the affine-bundle surjectivity of Stacks Lemma 42.32.1, tag 02TT); alternatively use the explicit principal divisors $\operatorname{div}(x-a)$ and $\operatorname{div}(y-b)$ of the coordinate functions on the lines through a point, which kill every point and every curve class. Injectivity in the induction: $\ker i_*$ is generated by $[\mathbb P^{d-1}]$? the computation is standard (Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.8-1.9 and Example 1.9.3; Vakil 245 Class 11; Cela, *Intersection Theory* Lecture 4). The degree formula is the $d=0$ case read off from the presentation, with $[x]=[\kappa(x):k][\mathbb P^0]$ obtained by pushing forward a closed point along the flat pullback to the line through it.

items.statement: For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with complement $u:U\hookrightarrow T$, $A_m(Z)\xrightarrow{j_*}A_m(T)\xrightarrow{u^*}A_m(U)\to0$ is exact. Projection $T\times\mathbb A^r\to T$ gives an isomorphism $A_m(T)\cong A_{m+r}(T\times\mathbb A^r)$. These statements hold for finite type schemes over a field and locally finite cycles on locally finite type schemes.
items.local_argument: Source: Stacks 42.19.3, 42.32 and 42.36.3. For localization, close each integral cycle of $U$ in $T$ to prove surjectivity. If the restriction of a cycle is a sum of principal divisors, close their supporting integral subvarieties in $T$ and extend the same rational functions; their divisors restrict to the specified divisors on $U$. Subtracting them leaves a cycle supported on $Z$, proving exactness. This also proves that locally finite sums can be used. For $\mathbb A^1_T$, surjectivity of pullback is proved on each integral cycle $V$: if $V$ is the whole line over its integral image, it is a pullback; otherwise over the generic point of its image it is the divisor of a polynomial in the line coordinate, and subtracting that principal divisor leaves cycles over a smaller closed subset. Noetherian induction finishes. Pullback is injective since the Cartier Gysin for the zero section is a left inverse (on a pulled-back cycle it cuts the coordinate by a nonzerodivisor and gives its original fundamental cycle). Iterate this argument for $\mathbb A^r_T$.  For injectivity in rank $r$, compose the Cartier Gysins of the $r$ coordinate-zero divisors; each cuts the corresponding polynomial coordinate on every pulled-back integral cycle and their composition is a left inverse. This is an argument with divisor Gysin only, independent of higher-codimension Gysin or Chern classes.

items.statement: For a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ with ideal $\mathcal I$, put $C_XY=\operatorname{Spec}_X(\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1})$ and $M=\operatorname{Bl}_{X\times\{\infty\}}(Y\times\mathbb P^1)$. Let $B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$ be the strict transform of $Y\times\{\infty\}$. The fibre at infinity is the sum $M_\infty=B+\mathbb P(C_XY\oplus1)$ of effective Cartier divisors, whose intersection is $\mathbb P(C_XY)$; this is a union with a common boundary, not a disjoint union. Projectivized cones here use the lines convention $\operatorname{Proj}(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathcal I}\mathcal O_Y[S])$. Off infinity $M\cong Y\times\mathbb A^1$, and $D_i:=M\setminus B$ has special fibre $C_XY$ and ordinary fibres $Y$. It is flat over $\mathbb P^1$. The specialization $\sigma_i:A_m(Y)\to A_m(C_XY)$ is obtained by extending the flat pullback of a cycle to $D_i$, then taking Cartier Gysin at infinity. It sends an integral $[V]$ to the fundamental cycle $[C_{X\cap V}V]$ pushed to $C_XY$. For a regular immersion of codimension $d$, the normal cone equals the rank-$d$ normal bundle $N_{X/Y}$. The construction works for finite type schemes over a field, with locally finite cycles in the locally finite type case.
items.local_argument:
Candidate source locators: Stacks 42.53 and 42.48.1, with Vakil Class14 as a sketch comparison only. Near infinity write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and let $t$ vanish at infinity. The $t$-chart of the blowup has ring $A[t,I/t]=\sum_{n\ge0}t^{-n}I^n[t]\subset A[t,t^{-1}]$. Multiplication by $t$ is injective and its quotient is $\operatorname{gr}_I A$. In the chart of a generator $a\in I$, the ring is $A[I/a][t/a]$ (the affine blowup algebra means the subring of $A_a$, including its usual torsion removal); $t=a(t/a)$, so its fibre is the sum of the exceptional divisor $a=0$ and the strict transform $t/a=0$. The strict transform charts are exactly $\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, and its intersection with the exceptional divisor is $\operatorname{Proj}\operatorname{gr}_I A$. This proves the fibre and open-chart assertions, even for singular $Y$. The charts embed in $A[t,t^{-1}]$ or are polynomial rings over the affine blowup algebras, and are torsion-free as $k[t]$-modules; all nonzero polynomials act injectively. A torsion-free module over the PID $k[t]$ is flat (every finitely generated submodule is free and the module is their filtered union). The infinity charts and ordinary product charts thus prove flatness without assuming $Y$ integral or misidentifying the centre as Cartier.
Localization gives a lift of the pulled-back class to $D_i$; two lifts differ by a class supported on $C_XY$. Cartier Gysin kills this difference because the normal line to the infinity fibre is trivial: $j^!j_*\gamma=c_1(1)\gamma=0$. Thus specialization is well defined on Chow classes. On $[V]$, closure in the $t$-chart is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_V[t,I\mathcal O_V/t]$; cutting by $t$ produces $\operatorname{gr}_{I\mathcal O_V}\mathcal O_V$, giving the asserted cone cycle with its generic lengths. For a regular sequence, the monomials in its generators identify $\operatorname{gr}_I A$ with $\operatorname{Sym}_{A/I}(I/I^2)$, hence the cone is $N_{X/Y}$.

items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$, and let $\mathcal E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of rank $r\ge1$ ([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Let
$$\pi:\mathbb P(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Proj}_X\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\longrightarrow X$$
be the projective bundle in the quotient convention, with tautological quotient $\pi^*\mathcal E\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(\mathcal E)}(1)$ ([[def-projective-bundle-scheme]], [[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]], [[thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients]]), and put $\xi:=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ ([[def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class]]); $\pi$ is smooth of relative dimension $r-1$ ([[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]]), so flat pullback $\pi^*$ is defined ([[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]], [[lem-smooth-fibres-smooth]]). Then for every $d\in\mathbb Z$ the map
$$\bigoplus_{i=0}^{r-1}A_{d+i}(X)\longrightarrow A_{d+r-1}\bigl(\mathbb P(\mathcal E)\bigr),\qquad (\alpha_0,\dots,\alpha_{r-1})\longmapsto\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}\xi^i\cap\pi^*\alpha_i,$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups. More precisely, $\pi_*(\xi^s\cap\pi^*\alpha)=0$ for $s<r-1$ and $\pi_*(\xi^{r-1}\cap\pi^*\alpha)=\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in A_*(X)$ ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]).

No smoothness of $X$ is assumed; if $X$ is smooth equidimensional of dimension $n$ then $\mathbb P(\mathcal E)$ is smooth equidimensional and the formula is a statement about the codimension-graded Chow groups $A^*(X)$, $A^*(\mathbb P(\mathcal E))$.
items.local_argument: Stacks42.36.1-36.2, full proof locators; final certification remains owner-held. For $\alpha=[V]$, choose $r-1$ independent sections in a trivialization over its generic point: successive hyperplanes leave a section, whose pushforward is $[V]$. Each smaller hyperplane power has positive-dimensional fibres and pushes to zero. Any difference from choosing the generic trivialization is supported on a smaller closed subset, and induction plus the $c_1$ projection formula proves these identities globally. For injectivity of the displayed map push down to get $\alpha_{r-1}=0$, then multiply by $\xi$ and push to get $\alpha_{r-2}=0$, continuing down to $\alpha_0$. For surjectivity, reduce to integral $X$ by pushforward from its components. Trivialize $E$ on a dense open $U$. For $U\times\mathbb P^{r-1}$, stratify projective space into affine spaces; localization and affine homotopy invariance give generators $[\mathbb P^j]$ pulled from classes of $U$. Each generator is a hyperplane power times $\pi^*$ by repeated Cartier cutting, so the displayed map is surjective over $U$. Lift its coefficients to $X$ by localization. The residual class is supported over $X\setminus U$; induction on the dimension of the integral image proves surjectivity there, and push-pull brings it to $X$. This argument is valid without a Chow ring on $X$: $\xi$ is a first Chern cap operator and the displayed direct-sum map is an isomorphism of groups, not a module over an undefined ring.

items.statement: For $f:Z\to T$, a degree-$d$ bivariant Chow operation assigns to every locally finite type $T'\to T$ homomorphisms $c:A_m(T')\to A_{m-d}(Z\times_TT')$, commuting with proper pushforward, flat pullback of fixed relative dimension, and Cartier divisor Gysin. Restriction along any base morphism, composition, and proper pushforward of such operations are defined by their action. Flat pullback and proper pushforward give bivariant operations, as does Cartier divisor Gysin. Equality can be tested on fundamental classes of integral schemes over $T$; it suffices to test after a proper birational modification of each such integral scheme.
items.local_argument: Source: Stacks 42.29-42.35. Composition commutes with each of the three operations by applying the relevant axiom first to its inner and then its outer factor; restriction merely changes the indexing family. Proper pushforward gives the same property by cartesian push-pull and the divisor projection formula. Flat pullback does so by flat composition and cartesian push-pull. For divisor Gysin, proper/flat compatibility is checked on integral cycles using the order/length definition when the cycle is not contained in the divisor, and $c_1(L)$ when it is; two Cartier Gysins commute. To verify the last assertion, when neither divisor contains the cycle their two cuts agree away from their common codimension-two locus, and the discrepancy at that locus is the principal-divisor boundary of the tame symbol $(-1)^{\operatorname{ord}a\operatorname{ord}b}a^{\operatorname{ord}b}/b^{\operatorname{ord}a}$; the one-dimensional order-function key lemma proves its divisor zero in the Chow quotient. When a cycle is contained in one divisor, the operation is $c_1$ of that line bundle and commutation reduces to commutation of two first Chern operations, proved by the same rational-section argument. This supplies the Cartier axiom without higher Gysin. For the equality criterion, every cycle is a finite sum of pushforwards of integral fundamental classes; commute $c$ with these pushforwards. If $h:V'\to V$ is proper birational and integral, $h_*[V']=[V]$, so equality on $[V']$ pushes to equality on $[V]$. This is a descent test for operations, not an assertion that Chow pullback to the modification is injective.

items.statement: Every rank-$r$ vector bundle $E$ on a finite type scheme $T$ has operators $c_j(E):A_m(T')\to A_{m-j}(T')$ for every $T'\to T$, defined by the projective bundle relation and commuting with the bivariant operations. They satisfy $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, $c(L)=1+c_1(L)$, arbitrary base restriction, $c(E)=c(E')c(E'')$ for $0\to E'\to E\to E''\to0$, and a splitting principle by iterated projective bundles whose flat pullback is injective after every base change. If a section of $E$ on a pure $n$ dimensional scheme $T$ has zero scheme regularly embedded of codimension $r$, then $c_r(E)\cap[T]=[Z(s)]$ in $A_{n-r}(T)$. These are operators on singular schemes; a Chow ring is not required.
items.local_argument:
Sources: Stacks 42.37-42.44. For every base $T'$ and cycle $\alpha$, use the unique projective bundle expansion to define $c_j(E)\cap\alpha$ by $\sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^j\xi^{r-j}\cap\pi^*(c_j(E)\cap\alpha)=0$. All terms have the same dimension; uniqueness follows from the basis and existence by expanding $\xi^r\pi^*\alpha$. Commuting any proper, flat or divisor operation through this equation and cancelling the basis proves the corresponding compatibility. More generally for any bivariant operation $b$ the projective bundle square and $b\xi=\xi b$ give $b c_j(E)=c_j(E)b$. A line bundle gives $\xi=c_1(L)$.
For Whitney, first if $0\to1\to E\to F\to0$, $\mathbb P(F)\subset\mathbb P(E)$ is the divisor of the induced section of $\mathcal O(1)$. Push its defining degree-$r-1$ relation to $\mathbb P(E)$: this gives the degree-$r$ relation with coefficients $c_j(F)$ and last coefficient zero. Uniqueness gives $c(E)=c(F)$. For a line subbundle $L$, twist by $L^{-1}$. The identity $\mathbb P(E\otimes L^{-1})=\mathbb P(E)$ shifts $\xi$ to $\xi-c_1(L)$; expanding its powers by the binomial formula transforms the relations into $c_j(E)=c_j(F)+c_1(L)c_{j-1}(F)$. This is uniquely forced degree by degree because the coefficient of $c_j(E)$ is one. For higher-rank subbundle $E'$, pull to $\mathbb P(E')$ with kernel $H$ and line quotient $L$; set $Q=\pi^*E/H$, which is an extension of $\pi^*E''$ by $L$. Induction gives $c(\pi^*E)=c(H)c(Q)=c(H)c(L)c(\pi^*E'')=c(\pi^*E')c(\pi^*E'')$; injectivity of projective bundle pullback descends the identity. Iterating kernels yields filtrations by lines; this construction applies to a finite family simultaneously and remains injective after any base change. This proves the splitting principle after Whitney, with no circular deduction from a filtration whose additivity has not yet been proved.
For the section formula use induction on $r$, the Cartier case being $r=1$. On $\mathbb P(E)$ let $t$ be the image of $s$ in $\mathcal O(1)$ and $H$ the kernel of $\pi^*E\to\mathcal O(1)$. On $Z(t)$ the section lifts to $H$ with zero scheme $\pi^{-1}Z(s)$. At its generic points the original regular sequence is transformed by an invertible change of generators to $t$ and $r-1$ generators, so they remain regular. The divisor $Z(t)$ has dimension $n+r-2$ and is generically Cartier: away from a whole projective fibre its equation is a nonzero linear polynomial; a whole fibre could be generic in this dimension only over a point of $Z(s)$ of dimension $n-1$, impossible since $\dim Z(s)=n-r$ and $r>1$. Thus the Cartier section formula and induction give $c_r(\pi^*E)[\mathbb P(E)]=c_{r-1}(H)[Z(t)]=[\pi^{-1}Z(s)]$. Injective $\pi^*$ gives the result.

items.statement: For any rank-$r$ vector bundle $p:E\to T$, flat pullback $p^*:A_m(T)\to A_{m+r}(E)$ is bijective, including after every base change. Its inverse is denoted $s_E^!$.
items.local_argument: Stacks 42.36.3. Compactify $E$ using the quotient-convention bundle $q:\mathbb P(E^\vee\oplus1)\to T$. The infinity divisor is $j:\mathbb P(E^\vee)\to\mathbb P(E^\vee\oplus1)$, with divisor class $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ from the trivial summand; its complement is $E$. Localization gives $A_*(\mathbb P(E^\vee))\xrightarrow{j_*}A_*(\mathbb P(E^\vee\oplus1))\to A_*(E)\to0$. The projective bundle basis on the source has $1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^{r-1}$, and on the target $1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^r$. Cartier cutting gives $j_*\pi^*\alpha=\xi q^*\alpha$ for every cycle (both sides are the zero of the trivial-summand section on the pulled-back cycle). By the $c_1$ projection formula, $j_*(\xi^a\pi^*\alpha)=\xi^{a+1}q^*\alpha$. Therefore the image of $j_*$ is precisely the positive-$\xi$ summands, leaving the $q^*$ summand as quotient. Restriction of $q^*$ is $p^*$, proving the isomorphism and its grading. This computation applies verbatim after any base change, since both bundles and their bases pull back.

items.statement: A section $s$ of a rank-$d$ bundle $Q$ whose zero scheme is cut out locally by a regular sequence has exact Koszul resolution $\bigwedge^dQ^\vee\to\cdots\to Q^\vee\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_{Z(s)}\to0$. Tensoring with a vector bundle preserves it. If a coherent sheaf $H$ has a finite locally free resolution on a scheme and $t$ is a Cartier equation acting injectively on $H$, restricting the resolution to $t=0$ remains exact and resolves $H/tH$. In the deformation blowup for a closed embedding of smooth quasi-projective varieties, the strict transform $F:X\times\mathbb P^1\hookrightarrow M$ is disjoint from $B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, and a resolution of $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ restricts exactly to the ordinary $Y$ fibre and to $P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(N\oplus1)$; on $B$ it is an exact complex.
items.local_argument:
Koszul exactness follows by induction on the regular sequence: the complex on $(a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ is the mapping cone of multiplication by $a_d$ on the complex on $(a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1})$. Its long exact homology sequence leaves only degree zero because $a_d$ is injective on $A/(a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1})$, with quotient $A/(a_1,\ldots,a_d)$. Exterior powers and contraction by $s$ are canonical under change of local frames, so these local resolutions glue. For fibre restriction, the two-term free resolution $[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{t}\mathcal O]$ of $\mathcal O/(t)$ shows that $\operatorname{Tor}_1(H,\mathcal O/(t))=\ker(t:H\to H)=0$ and all higher Tors vanish. Therefore derived tensor of any locally free resolution has homology only $H/tH$, proving ordinary restriction is exact. One must check $H$, not merely the ambient scheme, is flat or $t$-torsion-free.
For the smooth deformation, étale locally on $Y$, the embedding is given by coordinate regular sequence $a_1,\ldots,a_d$. The blowup charts of $(a_1,\ldots,a_d,t)$ are smooth: the $t$-chart has coordinates $u_j=a_j/t,t$ plus coordinates on $X$, and the $a_j$-charts have the ratios $a_l/a_j,t/a_j$ plus $a_j$ and the remaining smooth coordinates. This follows by base change from the corresponding affine-space charts, using the local smooth conormal sequence to choose étale coordinates. Thus $M$ is smooth, quasi-projective and has finite locally free coherent resolutions by the named K-theory supplier. The strict transform of $X\times\mathbb P^1$ is isomorphic to that scheme (its centre is its Cartier infinity divisor); at infinity it lies entirely in the $t$-chart, at $u_1=\cdots=u_d=0$. It meets $P$ at the section $[0:1]$ and misses $B$, which meets $P$ in $\mathbb P(N)$. On this chart $P$ has equation $t$, which acts injectively on $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ since that sheaf is the vector bundle on $X\times\mathbb P^1$. The ordinary fibre equation is likewise injective. The restriction lemma proves exactness on $P$ and on $Y$. Since the sheaf is zero near $B$, its resolution restricts to an exact complex there: locally an exact bounded complex of vector bundles resolving zero is split exact, by induction starting at its last cokernel. These calculations fill the flatness and component restriction omissions in Vakil19.

items.statement: For a rank-$r$ vector bundle $p:N\to T$, let $s_N^!=(p^*)^{-1}$. If $0\to N'\to N\to Q\to0$ is exact and $a:N'\hookrightarrow N$ is the vector subbundle immersion, then $s_N^!a_*p'^*\alpha=c_{\operatorname{rank}Q}(Q)\cap\alpha$. In particular $s_N^!s_*\alpha=c_r(N)\cap\alpha$. These identities and proper/flat/divisor compatibility hold after every base change.
items.local_argument: Sources: Stacks 42.44.2 and 42.36.3. Proper, flat and divisor compatibility of $s_N^!$ follows by applying the bijection $p^*$ and the corresponding push-pull or Cartier identity to each desired equality. The universal section of $p^*Q$ on $N$ is the image of its vector coordinate under $N\to Q$; its zero scheme is $N'$. For every integral $V\subset T$, its inverse image in $N$ is integral; this section cuts a polynomial regular sequence of $\operatorname{rank}Q$ fibre coordinates after a local splitting of the bundle sequence, so the regular-section formula gives $a_*p'^*[V]=c_{\operatorname{rank}Q}(p^*Q)p^*[V]=p^*(c_{\operatorname{rank}Q}(Q)[V])$. Linearity and bijective $p^*$ prove the displayed equality. Put $N'=0$ to obtain the zero-section/self-intersection formula. All splittings here are local and used to verify regularity only, not to assert a global bundle splitting.

items.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth quasi-projective over a field and $E$ a rank-$r$ bundle. For $q:P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(E)\to Y$, $K^0(P)=G_0(P)$ is generated as a $K^0(Y)$-module by $\mathcal O(a)$, $0\le a<r$. For $a\ge0$, $q_!\mathcal O(a)=\operatorname{Sym}^a(E^\vee)$. This statement has the corresponding dual form for quotient projective bundles.
items.local_argument: Use the relative diagonal in $P\times_YP$. Let $L_1=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal O(-1)$ and $Q_2$ the pullback of the tautological quotient of $q^*E$. The diagonal is the zero scheme of $L_1\to Q_2$, a regular section of $L_1^\vee\otimes Q_2$ of rank $r-1$: on the usual affine charts its equations are the differences of the $r-1$ affine fibre coordinates. Its exact Koszul resolution has terms $\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal O(-j)\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*\bigwedge^jQ^\vee$. For a vector bundle $H$ on $P$, tensor the resolution with $\operatorname{pr}_1^*H$ and push by $\operatorname{pr}_2$. The diagonal term pushes to $H$, so the K projection formula and flat base change for $q$ give $[H]=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}(-1)^j q^*(q_!(H(-j)))\,[\bigwedge^jQ^\vee]$. Base change here is the product projective-bundle square and can be verified on the standard projective affine cover: its Čech complexes tensor along the flat bundle projection, so their cohomology classes agree. From $0\to Q^\vee\to q^*E^\vee\to\mathcal O(1)\to0$, the exterior filtration identity gives $[\bigwedge^jQ^\vee]=\sum_{a=0}^j(-1)^a q^*[\bigwedge^{j-a}E^\vee][\mathcal O(a)]$. Thus each diagonal resolution term lies in the span of $\mathcal O(0),\ldots,\mathcal O(r-1)$, proving generation. Coherent sheaves reduce to vector bundles by finite resolution on the smooth quasi-projective $P$. For $a\ge0$, the local projective-space cohomology calculation has only degree-zero cohomology with its homogeneous monomial basis; changes of trivialization act by $\operatorname{Sym}^a(E^\vee)$, proving the pushforward formula globally, with higher direct images zero. This argument is a local completion of the general-bundle extension mentioned in the original scaffold; it uses no Riemann-Roch theorem.

items.statement: For a closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow T$ with a surjection $N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ from a rank-$d$ bundle on $Z$, each $T'\to T$ gives $Z'=Z\times_TT'$, a closed cone embedding $a:C_{Z'}T'\hookrightarrow N'=N|_{Z'}$, and an operation $c(Z,T,N):=(p'^*)^{-1}a_*\sigma_{Z'/T'}:A_m(T')\to A_{m-d}(Z')$. This family is bivariant and compatible with arbitrary base restriction. If $N'_{0}\subset N'$ is a vector subbundle through which the cone embedding factors, replacing $N'$ by $N'_{0}$ multiplies the operation by the top Chern operator of $N'/N'_{0}$.
items.local_argument: Sources: Stacks 42.48.1-48.3 and 42.54.1-54.5, full text retrieved; final source-to-argument certification remains owner-held. The ideal generating $Z'$ is $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$, so its powers are generated by the images of powers of $\mathcal I$; hence $\operatorname{Sym}(N'^\vee)\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}}\mathcal O_{T'}$. This proves the cone embedding for arbitrary, including nonflat, base change. For a proper $W\to\mathbb P^1_T$ isomorphic over $\mathbb A^1_T$, define infinity specialization on each base by lifting $\mathbb A^1$ pullback and applying Cartier Gysin at infinity. Localization and the trivial fibre normal line make the lift irrelevant. To commute it with a proper map, push forward any lift; its restriction is the proper push of the original pullback, and Cartier Gysin commutes with pushforward. To commute with flat pullback, pull back the lift and use flat/Cartier compatibility. To commute with a Cartier divisor Gysin, apply that Gysin to the lift and use commutation of Cartier Gysins; its ordinary restriction is the lift of the desired input. These arguments prove each bivariant axiom without an unspecified diagram chase. If a proper $W_1\to W_2$ is an isomorphism over the ordinary part, pushing a lift from $W_1$ to $W_2$ proves equality of their infinity operations after pushforward. Under nonflat base change, the blowup of $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$ has a closed immersion into the base change of the original blowup, induced by the surjection of Rees algebras, and is an isomorphism over the ordinary part. The preceding proper comparison therefore shows that the cone portions give the same class after pushforward to $N'$. Proper pushforward, open restriction and $(p'^*)^{-1}$ are bivariant, proving the claim. If the cone factors through $N'_0$, apply the vector subbundle identity of [[lem-zero-section-gysin-and-excess-vector-subbundle]] to its specialization class (write that class as $p_0^*\beta$ by homotopy invariance). This gives the excess factor exactly.

items.statement: The operations $c(Z,T,N)$ of [[lem-gysin-specialization-bivariant-and-base-change]] commute with every bivariant operation. Given $Z\subset Y\subset T$ and virtual normal bundles fitting into $0\to N_{Z/Y}\to N_{Z/T}\to N_{Y/T}|_Z\to0$ compatible with the conormal maps, $c(Z,T,N_{Z/T})=c(Z,Y,N_{Z/Y})c(Y,T,N_{Y/T})$. For regular embeddings this yields $(j i)^!=i^!j^!$, after all base changes. If a regular embedding is followed by a smooth projection, its Gysin likewise composes with the projection pullback; in particular a regular section of a smooth morphism gives $s^!p^*=1$.
items.local_argument:
Sources: Stacks 42.54.8-54.10 and 42.59.1-59.6. Test equality on integral $T'\to T$, allowing proper birational modification by the bivariant criterion. If its inverse image of $Z$ is all of $T'$, the cone is the zero section and $c$ is the top Chern operator by [[lem-zero-section-gysin-and-excess-vector-subbundle]], hence central. Otherwise blow up the nonzero ideal of the inverse image of $Z$. The new inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor; the pulled-back virtual normal bundle surjects onto its normal line and the kernel is a vector bundle $Q$ (dually the conormal surjection has locally free kernel). The excess formula gives $c=c_{\mathrm{top}}(Q)D^!$. Both factors commute with every bivariant operation, respectively by [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]] and the Cartier axiom. Proper pushforward of the fundamental class proves commutation on the original integral base. Thus no unproved Gysin commutation is used.
For composition, use the same equality criterion and blow up the product of the two nonzero ideals to make both inverse images Cartier; invertibility of a product ideal implies invertibility of its factors locally on this blowup, since each factor generates an invertible fractional ideal. If an inverse image is the entire base, the identity reduces directly to the excess vector subbundle formula. In the Cartier case split off the excess bundle for $Y/T$ using the two exact sequences. Centrality of its top Chern operation reduces the question to the case that $N_{Y/T}$ is the normal line to $Y$ in $T$. Denote its zero section by $o:Y\to C_YT$. The essential cone identity is $o^![C_ZT]=[C_ZY]$ as a class in $A_{n-1}(C_ZT\times_{C_YT}Y)$ for integral $T$ of dimension $n$. Here is its local justification, filling the calculation omitted in Stacks54.9: if the Cartier ideals are $(a)$ for $Z$ and $(b)$ for $Y$, the inclusion $Z\subset Y$ gives $b=ac$. The open deformation ring for $Z$ is $A[t,a/t]\subset A[t,t^{-1}]$, and the ring for $Y$ maps to it by $b/t\mapsto c(a/t)$. Hence there is a morphism of open deformation spaces, including their special cones. The strict transform of $Y\times\mathbb P^1$ in the $Z$ blowup is the blowup of $Y\times\mathbb P^1$ in $Z\times\{\infty\}$: on affine charts this is the quotient by the saturation of $(b)$ with respect to the exceptional equation. Its cone part at infinity is therefore $C_ZY$. The Cartier divisor on the $Y$ deformation given by its vertex section restricts on the ordinary part to $Y\subset T$; its pullback cut of the $Z$ deformation agrees there with the strict transform. Differences are supported at infinity, so infinity Gysin kills them. Cartier commutation now gives $o^![C_ZT]=[C_ZY]$. This also treats the component contained in the divisor using the Cartier $c_1$ rule, rather than treating $cu=0$ as always a regular equation. In the vector-bundle square $N_{Z/Y}\subset N_{Z/T}\to N_{Y/T}|_Z$, Cartier Gysin for the kernel commutes with bundle pullback and sends the first cone class to the second by this identity. Apply the two inverse bundle pullbacks: they characterize precisely the two sides of the composition formula, so they agree. Push down the modifications to finish.
Finally, for a regular immersion $s:Z\hookrightarrow P$ with $P\to T$ smooth and $Z\to T$ flat of the expected dimension, each flat pullback of an integral $[V]$ has normal cone to $Z\times_TV$ equal to the normal bundle of $s$ restricted there. Locally the regular equations remain a regular sequence on this pullback: smooth coordinates and flatness of $Z/T$ imply Tor independence, by the local flatness criterion. Specialization gives its full normal bundle fundamental cycle; inverse bundle pullback gives $[Z\times_TV]$. This proves $s^!p^*=(ps)^*$, including the section case $ps=1$. Factor two graph presentations through their product over the base and apply the established immersion composition and this smooth identity; it proves independence and composition of graph Gysin for morphisms between smooth schemes. All normal-bundle equalities used in this argument are exact sequences, not global splittings.

items.statement:
Let $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be a regular closed embedding of codimension $d$ with normal bundle $N$. In particular a closed embedding of smooth schemes of constant codimension is regular. For any $f:Y'\to Y$, put $X'=X\times_YY'$ and $N'=N|_{X'}$. The pulled-back ideal gives a closed immersion $a:C_{X'}Y'\hookrightarrow N'$. Define
$$i^!_{Y'}=(p'^*)^{-1}a_*\sigma_{X'/Y'}:A_m(Y')\longrightarrow A_{m-d}(X'),$$
using [[def-deformation-to-the-normal-cone-and-specialization]] and [[lem-vector-bundle-chow-homotopy-invariance]]. No fibre product of deformation spaces over $\mathbb P^1$ with a fictitious map to $Y$ is used. The same construction for a regular locally closed embedding uses restriction to an open in which it is closed; the operations agree under further restriction and extension of cycles, so this is intrinsic.
For $h:Y''\to Y'$ and $h_X:X''=X\times_YY''\to X'$, properness of $h$ gives $i^!_{Y'}h_*=(h_X)_*i^!_{Y''}$, and flatness of $h$ gives $i^!_{Y''}h^*=h_X^*i^!_{Y'}$. These do not require the base-changed embedding to be regular. If $X'\hookrightarrow Y'$ is regular with normal bundle $N_0\subset N'$ and excess bundle $Q=N'/N_0$, then $i^!_{Y'}=c_{d-\operatorname{rank}N_0}(Q)\cap (i')^!$. In particular $i^!i_*\alpha=c_d(N)\cap\alpha$. Here $c_j$ means the already defined operational Chern operator of [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]]; it later becomes the Chow-ring Chern class on a smooth scheme. Codimension-one Gysin equals Cartier divisor Gysin; refined Gysins commute, and $(ji)^!=i^!j^!$ for composed regular embeddings. They commute with Chern cap operations. For any operational class $c$ on $Y$ and $\beta\in A_*(X)$, its projection formula is $i_*(c|_X\cap\beta)=c\cap i_*\beta$. Under the later smooth operational-ring identification this is the ring formula $i_*(i^*\alpha\cdot\beta)=\alpha\cdot i_*\beta$.
items.local_argument:
The construction and arbitrary-base-change bivariant axioms are proved in [[lem-gysin-specialization-bivariant-and-base-change]], with its excess vector subbundle formula. Self-intersection applies that formula to the base change $Y'=X$: the ideal is zero, its cone is the zero section, and the quotient bundle is $N$; use proper compatibility to identify this restricted operation with $i^!i_*$. For Cartier agreement, test on an integral base cycle. If it is not contained in the divisor, its cone is the normal line and the operation is its Cartier fundamental cycle; if contained, the zero-cone computation gives $c_1$ of the restricted normal line. These are exactly the two cases of Cartier Gysin. Commutation and composition, including the necessary cone calculation, are [[lem-refined-gysin-commutation-and-composition]]. Locality for locally closed embeddings follows from the same cone formula on every cycle and independence of a lift in specialization; in each overlap the identical ideal and normal bundle give identical operators. The operational projection formula is the proper axiom of a bivariant class; its ring interpretation is provided by the later smooth-ring theorem, and is not a prerequisite for this construction.
